Calculate the discriminant (b² - 4ac) to see if there are real solutions. If positive, two real roots; if zero, one root; if negative, complex roots. Plug in the values and simplify. To find stationary points, first take the derivative f'(x). Set f'(x) = 0 and solve for x. These x-values are candidates for stationary points. Plug them back into the original function to get y-values. Then, use the second derivative test: if f''(x) > 0, it’s a local minimum; if f''(x) < 0, a local maximum. This helps identify where the function changes direction.
